title: Integrate tone guard and softener into delay voice in binding order
description:
Wire RepeatToneProcessor, PresenceGuard, and RepeatTransientSoftener into Source/DSP/DelayVoice.h and Source/DSP/DelayVoice.cpp, and register the three new module source files in CMakeLists.txt.

Before editing, inspect:
- Source/DSP/DelayVoice.h and Source/DSP/DelayVoice.cpp (existing per-sample feedback loop, prepare/reset signatures, delay line read/write, feedback tap)
- Source/DSP/RepeatToneProcessor.h (from d.1: prepare, setHighPassFrequency, setLowPassFrequency, processHighPassSample, processLowPassSample, updateCoefficients)
- Source/DSP/PresenceGuard.h (from d.2: prepare, processSample, updateCoefficients, setEffectiveMaxCutDb)
- Source/DSP/RepeatTransientSoftener.h (from d.3: prepare, processSample, updateCoefficients, setAmountPercent)
- CMakeLists.txt (the existing target_sources list for the plugin target and the test runner target)

Required integration — the repeat-loop order inside each voice's feedback loop is binding and must appear in exactly this order:
1. fractional delay read
2. HPF (RepeatToneProcessor::processHighPassSample)
3. LPF (RepeatToneProcessor::processLowPassSample)
4. Presence Guard (PresenceGuard::processSample)
5. repeat transient softener (RepeatTransientSoftener::processSample)
6. mild saturation — RESERVED SLOT for phase e: leave a clearly marked pass-through comment placeholder only, implement nothing
7. restricted diffusion — RESERVED SLOT for phase e: leave a clearly marked pass-through comment placeholder only, implement nothing
8. feedback tap

Rules:
- Add the three processors as by-value members of DelayVoice; call their prepare() from DelayVoice::prepare() and reset() from DelayVoice::reset().
- Call each processor's updateCoefficients() at the bounded control rate from the voice's block/control-rate boundary, not per sample.
- Delay read positions remain clamped to [8 samples, 8.25 seconds]; do not alter existing clamping.
- Feedback gain remains T60-derived g = 10^(-3*T/T60) with the hard cap g_final = min(g_requested, 0.985); do not change that logic.
- juce::ScopedNoDenormals stays at the top of the processor-level entry point; do not add allocation, locks, file IO, string construction, or buffer resizing to the audio path.
- In CMakeLists.txt, add Source/DSP/RepeatToneProcessor.cpp, Source/DSP/PresenceGuard.cpp, and Source/DSP/RepeatTransientSoftener.cpp to the existing plugin target source list (and to the test runner target's source list if that target compiles DSP sources directly). Do not add new targets, options, or third-party dependencies, and do not touch JUCE/ or the JUCE submodule pin.

This task does not create test files; tests are added in d.5.
acceptance_criteria: Source/DSP/DelayVoice.h declares RepeatToneProcessor, PresenceGuard, and RepeatTransientSoftener members by value
Source/DSP/DelayVoice.cpp calls prepare() and reset() on all three processors from DelayVoice::prepare() and DelayVoice::reset()
The per-sample feedback loop in Source/DSP/DelayVoice.cpp applies, in order: fractional delay read, high-pass, low-pass, presence guard, transient softener, then the feedback tap
Reserved comment placeholders for mild saturation and restricted diffusion appear between the softener and the feedback tap with no implementation
updateCoefficients() for all three processors is called at a control-rate or block boundary, not once per sample
Existing delay read clamping to [8 samples, 8.25 seconds] and the feedback cap g_final = min(g_requested, 0.985) are unchanged
CMakeLists.txt lists Source/DSP/RepeatToneProcessor.cpp, Source/DSP/PresenceGuard.cpp, and Source/DSP/RepeatTransientSoftener.cpp in the plugin target sources
No file outside the task's allowed_write_paths is created or modified
forbidden_changes: modify anything under JUCE/ or change the JUCE submodule pin

modify Source/DSP/RepeatToneProcessor.h, Source/DSP/RepeatToneProcessor.cpp, Source/DSP/PresenceGuard.h, Source/DSP/PresenceGuard.cpp, Source/DSP/RepeatTransientSoftener.h, or Source/DSP/RepeatTransientSoftener.cpp
